sentences.text: The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that: That on 28092022 at about 08.45 p.m, when the petitioner was riding the Honda Activa Bike bearing No.KA05HM166 proceeding from Channarayapatna to his house, near Channarayapatna - Shravanabelagola Road, near Janivara Manjanna House, at the same time, the driver of Lorry bearing No.AP39Y1269 belonging to the respondent No.1, without any signal or without switching on the indicator, loading the ginger inside of the lorry, due to which the said petitioner could not control the vehicle and dashed to back side of the said lorry.

Due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and was immediately shifted to Channarayapatna Government hospital, wherein after first aid as per the advise of the doctor, he was shifted to Vijayanagar hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient from 29.09.2022 to 26.10.2022 and has undergone operation and has spent Rs.15,00,000/ towards medical and other expenses and he is still under followup treatment as outpatient and prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 24 years and was employee at Navachethana Finance Pvt. Ltd., Channarayapatna and earning Rs.30,000/
p.m.
Due to accidental injuries he could not do his work from the date of accident and sustained loss of income and become permanent disabled.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry involved in the accident and in this regard the Channarayapatna Town Police have registered a case against driver of the said offending lorry.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. On service of summons, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appeared before the tribunal and hence, was placed exparte.

04. The respondent No.2, in its written statement denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits that this respondent is the insurer of Lorry bearing No.AP39Y1269 vide Policy No.56030131221 0000069 valid from 29.04.2022 to 28.04.2023 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is further denied age, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner.

The driver of the lorry did not having effective and valid driving licence and denied the permit and fitness certificate of the lorry as on the date of accident and as per Police records, lorry was parked before the house owner of goods for loading purpose, the petitioner riding his Honda Activa vehicle in rash and negligent and himself hit back side of lorry, due to Adithya C.A vs Gandla Ravi Kumar on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54535760/

The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties namely insurer of Honda Activa Bike bearing No.KA05HM166 has contributed to the alleged accident to an extent of 100% and the compensation claimed is exorbitant and hence, pray to dismiss the petition against this respondent.
05.
Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor:  ISSUES 01.

Whether the natural guardian of petitioner proves that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 28.09.2022 at about 08.45 p.m, on CR Patna, Shravanabelagola Road, near Janivara Manjanna House, Kasaba Hobli, CR Patna Taluk, Hassan.
due to negligent parking of Lorry bearing registration No. AP39Y1269 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?
06.

The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined his brother and natural guardian as PW.1 and got examined three witnesses i.e., MRI and the doctors who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability as PW.2 to 4 and got marked 29 documents as Ex.P.1 to 29 and closed his side evidence.
On behalf of the respondent No.2, its Administrative Officer got examined as RW.1 and through him 03 documents are marked as Ex.R.1 to 3 and closed its side evidence.
07. I have heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for petitioner and respondent No.2 and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as under: Issue No.1 In the Affirmative Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 As per final order for the following:
REASONS
09. Issue No.1:
The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined his brother and natural guardian as PW.1 and in his chiefexamination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
During the course of crossexamination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits the suggestion that the petitioner will have food when some one feed him.

The petitioner is not able to give evidence before this Court and he will speak only some basic sentences and doctor has given letter stating that the petitioner is incapable to give evidence and he can adduce the evidence of said doctor and admits that near the accident spot there was no such street lights and denied to the suggestion that the petitioner due to his rash riding hit against the loaded lorry and sustained injuries and denied to the suggestion that his brother has not sustained head injuries as stated in his petition and denied to the suggestion that the petitioner has not sustained any grievous injuries and the petitioner did not took any followup treatment after discharge and denied to the suggestion that the petitioner was not earning Rs.25,000/ p.m and denied to the suggestion that the petitioner is normal and capable of giving evidence and in order to suppress the real facts, he was Adithya C.A vs Gandla Ravi Kumar on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54535760/

sentences.text: On going through the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, the petitioner has clearly established and proved that the he sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 28092022 at about 08.45 p.m, near Channarayapatna - Shravanabelagola Road, near Janivara Manjanna House, due to negligent parking of Lorry bearing No.AP39Y1269 by its driver as alleged in the petition.
Therefore, the petitioner has proved the Issue No.1.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was aged about 24 years and was employee at Navachethana Finance Pvt. Ltd., Channarayapatna and earning Rs.30,000/ p.m and has incurred Rs.15,00,000/ towards medical and other expenses.
Due to accident he sustained grievous injuries and head injury and he was unable to do work and lost income, undergone mental agony and sufferings and became permanent disabled.

17. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth and he has not produced any evidence regarding his avocation and income.
But he has produced Ex.P.11 Aadhaar card and Ex.P.13 Driving licence of the petitioner, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 07.05.1998 and the alleged accident occurred on 28092022.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 24 years and the same is considered for calculating compensation.
As per Sarla Verma case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 is 18 and the same is considered.
18. As stated above with regard to avocation and income the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the LokAdalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2022 to be taken as Rs.15,500/ p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.15,500/.
19.

According to the evidence of PW.3, the doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and also head injury and he assessed whole body disability due to permanent physical impairment due to neurological conditions is 41% (mild disability) due to head injury.
Hence, considering the evidence of PW.3 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 41%.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.10 and 27 Discharge summaries, according to which the petitioner was admitted to Vijayanagar hospital, Bengaluru and Shri Dharmasthala Manjunatheshwara College of Ayurveda and hospital,
Hassan, as inpatient for totally for 35 days.

Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.50,000/ under this head.
21. Pain and sufferings:

As per Ex.P.8 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.3 doctor and Ex.P.20 Case sheet, Ex.P.21 Clinical notes, Ex.P.22 Neuro psychological assessment with work sheets, Ex.P.23 MRI brain report and Ex.P.29 is OPD and on account of accidental injuries petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.50,000/ under this head.
22. Loss of income during laid up period:

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.15,500/ p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for 35 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast one year.

Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.1,86,000/
(Rs.15,500 x 12) under this head.
23. Medical expenses:
As per Ex.P.14 the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.12,03,256/. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.12,03,256/ under the head of medical expenses.
24. Loss of future amenities in life and unhappiness:

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and the disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness,
the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.50,000/
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
25. Future medical expenses: The petitioner has not produced any documents with respect to future medical expenses and even PW.3 has not stated anything about future surgery or future treatment of the petitioner and no estimation is produced regarding future medical expenses.
Therefore
, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
26. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:

28. On behalf of the respondent No.2, its Administrative Officer is examined as RW.1, wherein in his chiefexamination evidence he has reiterated the written statement averments.

During the cross examination by the petitioner counsel he admits that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is valid and is in force and alleged accident occurred at night hours and also admits that Police after investigation has filed Charge sheet against the driver of the lorry for negligent parking of lorry.
Further, he has produced Ex.R.2 copy of Policy which is goods carriage vehicle package policy is valid from 29.04.2022 to 28.04.2023 and the alleged accident was occurred on 28.09.2022.
Therefore, it appears that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending lorry was valid and is in force.

29. Further, the respondent No.2 has relied upon the following citations to dismiss the claim petition against the respondent No.2:
01. ILR 2015 KAR 3017 in between Lalitha and another Vs N.Kedarnath and others 02. (2002) 6 SCC 455 in between Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri V/s Karmasey Kunvargi Tak and others 03. ILR 2007 KAR 914 in between Manjunatha V/s P.Shankar and another I have gone through the above citations relied by the respondent No.2 Insurance Company.

sentences.text: But under the facts and circumstances of the case, there is no evidence on record to show that the petitioner injured was also contributed for the accident.

In case if lorry driver has not parked his lorry on the middle of the road and in case if he has taken precautionary measures by keeping considerable distance while parking vehicles and using indicators, then accident may be avoided.
But the lorry driver is gross negligently has parked his lorry without indication and without taking precautionary measures in the middle of the road.
Since the accident is occurred in night hours and since lorry driver has not switched indicators or parking lights are not used, the accident was occurred.
Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner does not arise at all.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the RC Owner of the offending Lorry and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount with interest from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
30. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Due to accident he sustained grievous injuries and head injury and he was unable to do work and lost income, undergone mental agony and sufferings and became permanent disabled.
17. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth and he has not produced any evidence regarding his avocation and income.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast one year.
Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and the disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness,
the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.50,000/
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
25. Future medical expenses: The petitioner has not produced any documents with respect to future medical expenses and even PW.3 has not stated anything about future surgery or future treatment of the petitioner and no estimation is produced regarding future medical expenses.
Therefore, it appears that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending lorry was valid and is in force.
But under the facts and circumstances of the case, there is no evidence on record to show that the petitioner injured was also contributed for the accident.
In case if lorry driver has not parked his lorry on the middle of the road and in case if he has taken precautionary measures by keeping considerable distance while parking vehicles and using indicators, then accident may be avoided.
But the lorry driver is gross negligently has parked his lorry without indication and without taking precautionary measures in the middle of the road.
Since the accident is occurred in night hours and since lorry driver has not switched indicators or parking lights are not used, the accident was occurred.
Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner does not arise at all.
Hence, the respondent No.1 being the RC Owner of the offending Lorry and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount with interest from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
